column3: I'm up here investigating how we can reappropriate this plant for the City Restoration Project.
Or... I would be, but the room to the generator in the back seems to be locked.
I've already called down to the Grand Hall, and no one seems to have it.
And this building belonged to the Yureyu Company, so they would have the key, only...
There is the small problem that they no longer exist.
Maybe it's impossible after all...
\PN flashed the Yureyu key.

How in the world did you find it? This is wonderful!
You go ahead and unlock the place and have a look around and I'll report back to the city that we can make progress!
Oh! And hold onto this while you do.
I found it when I was digging around in there.
I'm not sure what it is, but it could be important.
Much obliged; take care!
Yureyu Power Plant

Unflinching power!
I will never stop fighting!!!

Well, you know.
But for those of us that are still here, it's just proof that we will never, ever bow out.
Willpower is putting one foot in front of the other, every day, even when it's the absolute last thing you want to do.
That's what Victoria taught me.
Let's show Kiki just how strong our willpower is!

VICTORIA: Perhaps,
But then, who is making the rules?
Now let's do something else.
First, I'll empty the bowl; we're starting over...
VICTORIA: Okay, now as you can see, I've filled the bowl with sand from the get-go.
Can I fit any rocks into this bowl?
HIKER: If it's specifically rocks, no. Surely not.
VICTORIA: Correct.
When we start with the rocks, there's room for the sand.
When we start with the sand, there's no room for rocks.
You can think of the sand as our everyday responsibilities.
Work, house chores, and so on.
If we prioritize them, we have no room for other things.
But if we prioritize the rocks, which we can think of as things we truly enjoy-- our passions and aspirations...
Well, the sand finds a way regardless, doesn't it?
YOUNGSTER: What about the water?
VICTORIA: The water...
I prefer to think of it as the people we care about.
There's always room for them.
RANGER: Excuse me?
VICTORIA: How can we help you?
RANGER: We're from the Johto Region...
Er, we heard something about some kind of famous spiritual counselor out here?
We were hoping to study with her.
VICTORIA: ...Ah, I'm sorry.
If you mean Kiki, I'm afraid she's no longer with us.
RANGER: No, no, no that ain't it--
Her name was, uh, Victoria?
VICTORIA: ...Oh?
Yes, that would be me.
Please, take a seat; you're very welcome!

KIKI: It is the nature of those precious few among us who truly care to pick up more responsibilities than we are able to uphold.
There is much to be said there, for personal boundaries, for managing the weight of these burdens, and prioritizing them in whichever way will saddle us with the fewest regrets.
But those are not concerns of the present moment.
For now, it is enough to simply acknowledge that these struggles exist.
They are there now, and for better or worse, they will be there later.
But their presence does not have to obstruct you from enjoying the benefits of a peaceful mental state in the meantime.

Even Kiki, for all her focus on wellness, couldn't outlast her expiration in any way that mattered!
KIKI: The physical clock ticks at the same speed for everyone; this is true.
And we none of us can prevent our varied ends.
But your mind does not subscribe to the speed of the second hand.
The clock is a tool measuring the rotation of planets; not the passing of thoughts.
Our mental states can do much to affect the rate at which our time passes, both in the moment and in our longer term health.
By calming oneself and putting the mind into a resting state, we can extend our mental and physical energies, and make the most of our time in all senses.
In order to speed up, one must slow down.
But these arguments do not need to be made now either.
You may simply acknowledge that the conflict exists within you, and without resolution, set it aside.
FELICIA: ...
VICTORIA: So, you heard the rumors too?
That Kiki is back.
And what a crowd she drew.
This turnout is easily double or triple any lecture I gave.
But what I really want to know...
Is why...
Why does she look like--
VICTORIA: Why does she look like me?!
KIKI: And break.
As you continue meditating, you will inevitably find thoughts and feelings bubble to the surface.
Though with practice the frequency decreases, this is only normal.
Acknowledge that you have had the thought or feeling, and then return your mind to a neutral state.
It is all too easy and common to be swept away in the tide of one's impulsive cognition, but there is no need to swim or struggle.
Let the thoughts wash around you, and then recede as you firmly maintain your ground.
We will begin again; please practice this.
KIKI: Remember, for beginners, it is okay to focus on your breathing rather than simply trying to think of nothing.
I see we have new guests in the back as well.
If you'd like, you may sit and join us in meditation,
And if you'd prefer to simply observe for today that's okay as well.
Now, silence.
VICTORIA: This is creepy and weird and I don't like it.
I'm not a "guest," I'm supposed to--
Ugh, and why does she look like me?!
And why does she know her lectures, and talk like her?
If this is someone's idea of a joke, I hate it more than anything!
KIKI: Our guests in the back should remain quiet so that the students may concentrate.

But this is so wrong! Kiki is--
I could just--
...Okay, no. She's right.

I will gather myself and wait.

Twelve o'clock, next to that girl?
VICTORIA: There, he just shifted again!

I bet he's lost in some train of thought right now and doesn't even realize it.
Part of me wants to go break his focus just to spite "Kiki".
It'd take some pestering, but he'd crack like an egg.
...But that's just petty. There's no need to do that.
For now, I'll just try to calm down, and then hopefully this can all be unwound reasonably.
VICTORIA: For now, I'll just try to calm down...
And resist the urge to pick on that guy in the center.
VICTORIA: I have no idea who that guy is.
I've never seen them around the Grand Hall before.
So him talking about leading both this place and Reborn is...
Where did that even come from?
And snapping right back to meditation with no further comment.
Something is really weird here!
I have a theory...
\PN, this is unorthodox, but let's keep bothering the students who are meditating!
Most of them might not crack, but I can spot the ones who will.

Wanna see if you can do it again?
VICTORIA: I think this about confirms my theory...
Those aren't the students' thoughts and concerns.
Those are mine.
Kiki has my face.
The crowd has my doubts.
I don't understand why this is happening, but I want it to stop.
This is humiliating on both accounts.
...The guy in blue at the front.
I saw him shift too.
...One of the people at the front.
I couldn't tell who, but I saw movement up there.
VICTORIA: The path is clear, then...
KIKI: You are correct.
You cannot be like me.
That is why I am here.
You no longer need to.
VICTORIA: That's-- not...
KIKI: Didn't you want to be relieved of your burdens?
Didn't you want to return to the days when you could live freely?
Was the responsibility not too much?
VICTORIA: Who even are you!?
What are you doing here?!
Did you come here just to embarrass me in front of everyone?!
Or are you just trying to control them?
Why would anyone want the responsibility if not for the power?
And even that's never enough to actually stop anyone!
Fat lot of good it did me when Team Meteor was here-- I was as powerless in Labradorra as I was atop Pyrous Mountain when you--
When you...
KIKI: Then you can simply let me take care of everything.
VICTORIA: No!
KIKI: For what purpose do you cling to the responsibility?
It is destroying you.
VICTORIA: Because this is my home, too!
I'm not handing it over to some stupid shadow clone who takes pleasure in humiliating others!
VICTORIA: \PN, please--
Put her out of my misery.
KIKI: Even now, she seeks someone else to do what she cannot.
But this fight is irrational.
I am already exactly what she desired to not have to be.
I am Kiki.
Please be at rest.
Your premise was wrong from the start.
KIKI: You cannot lead this place as I did.
The shoes you've been asked to fill will never fit.
You can never be me.
You can only be you.
You can lead this place in the way that only you are able to.
That will be enough.
